Then, in your Fragment class, you need to set the Toolbar as the ActionBar. Here's how you can do it: ```java import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity; import androidx.appcompat.widget.Toolbar; public class MyFragment extends Fragment { @Override public View onCreateView(LayoutInflater inflater, ViewGroup container, Bundle savedInstanceState) { View view = inflater.inflate(R.layout.fragment_my, container, false); Toolbar toolbar = (Toolbar) view.findViewById(R.id.toolbar); ((AppCompatActivity)getActivity()).setSupportActionBar(toolbar); // If you want to add a title ((AppCompatActivity)getActivity()).getSupportActionBar().setTitle("My Fragment"); return view; } } ``` Remember, you need to cast the getActivity() to AppCompatActivity before calling the setSupportActionBar() method. Also, if you want to add menu items to your toolbar, you need to override the onCreateOptionsMenu() method in your fragment and inflate the menu XML file. ```java @Override public void onCreateOptionsMenu(Menu menu, MenuInflater inflater) { inflater.inflate(R.menu.menu_main, menu); super.onCreateOptionsMenu(menu, inflater); } ``` Don't forget to call setHasOptionsMenu(true) in the onCreate() or onCreateView() method of your fragment. ```java @Override public void onCreate(Bundle savedInstanceState) { super.onCreate(savedInstanceState); setHasOptionsMenu(true); } ``` This is a basic way to add a toolbar in a fragment. Memory usage is a critical factor in the performance of AWS Lambda functions written in Node.js. When a Lambda function is executed, it is allocated a certain amount of memory, and the function must complete its execution within that memory limit. If the function exceeds its memory limit, it will be terminated and an error will be returned.

In general, the more memory a Lambda function uses, the slower it will perform. This is because the function will have to spend more time allocating and deallocating memory, which can slow down the execution of the function. Additionally, if the function uses too much memory, it may cause the Lambda service to run out of memory, which can cause other functions to be terminated.

To optimize the performance of a Lambda function written in Node.js, it is important to keep the memory usage as low as possible while still meeting the requirements of the function. This can be achieved by using efficient algorithms, minimizing the use of global variables, and avoiding the use of unnecessary libraries or modules.

It is also important to note that the amount of memory allocated to a Lambda function can affect its cost. The more memory a function uses, the higher its cost will be. Therefore, it is important to strike a balance between the performance requirements of the function and the cost of running it.<|eot_id|>
